'''Ken Baldwin''' (born 1954) is an Australian physicist who is professor of physics at the [[Australian National University]] (ANU). He is the deputy director of the [[ANU Research School of Physics|Research School of Physics]] and the director of the ANU Energy Change Institute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://researchers.anu.edu.au/researchers/baldwin-kgh|title=Professor Kenneth Baldwin|last=Director&nbsp;(Research&nbsp;Services&nbsp;Division)|website=researchers.anu.edu.au|access-date=2016-05-17}}</ref>

== Career ==
Ken Baldwin was born on 26 November 1954 in [[Canberra|Canberra, Australia]]. He completed a [[Bachelor of Science]] and a Master of Science at ANU, followed by a PhD at [[Imperial College London]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}}

Baldwin's main contributions as a research scientist pertain to two related fields of [[physics]]: the use of [[laser]] techniques (in particular the generation of vacuum [[ultraviolet radiation]] <200&nbsp;nm) for the precision measurement of atoms and molecules; and the use of laser cooling to trap and manipulate metastable helium atoms to study fundamental [[quantum physics]] and for precision measurement.{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}}

Baldwin has published over 100 refereed publications in experimental atomic, molecular and optical physics, as well as over 200 conference papers.{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}}

In 2007, Baldwin received the W.H. Beattie Steele Medal – the highest award of the Australian Optical Society. In 2010 he received the Barry Inglis Medal from the National Measurement Institute for "excellence in precision measurement."

Baldwin has played a leading role in optics in Australia, and from 1993 to 1994 he was president of the Australian Optical Society.

Baldwin served on the [[Australian Academy of Science National Committees|Australian Academy of Science]]'s National Committee for Spectroscopy (1996–2005), and the National Committee for Physics (2000–03, 2014–present).{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}}

He was the first Australian to chair the International Council on Quantum Electronics from 2002 to 2005, overseeing the premier world laser conference series IQEC.{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}}  In 2011 he chaired the IQEC/CLEO Pacific Rim conference in Sydney.

Baldwin was elected by the worldwide membership of the [[Optical society of america|Optical Society of America]] (OSA) to a 3-year term (2006–2008) as director at large of the OSA Board, the only time that an Australian has served in this capacity.{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}}

In 2010 Baldwin established the ANU Energy Change Institute (ECI) as its Founding Director.

In 2014 Baldwin chaired the OSA Congress on Light, Energy and the Environment in Canberra – the first time that this conference has been brought to Australia - and which featured Professor [[Steven Chu]], former Energy Secretary to President Barack Obama.{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}} As of 2016, his role as Chair is ongoing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.osa.org/en-us/meetings/optics_and_photonics_congresses/osa_light_energy_and_the_environment_congress/|title=Light, Energy and the Environment Congress|publisher=The Optical Society|access-date=2016-05-18}}</ref>

Baldwin is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], the Institute of Physics (UK), the Optical Society of America and the Australian Institute of Physics. He was elected a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Technology and Engineering]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Kenneth Baldwin FTSE|url=https://www.atse.org.au/news-and-events/article/kenneth-baldwin |publisher=Australian Academy of Technology & Engineering |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127040622/https://www.atse.org.au/news-and-events/article/kenneth-baldwin |archive-date=2021-11-27 |url-status=dead |access-date=2025-04-11}}</ref>

== Science policy ==
Baldwin has been a key contributor to science policy in Australia. He was elected as President in 2008–09 of the Federation of Australian Scientific and Technological Societies (the peak science advocacy group – now [[Science and Technology Australia]], and also served as FASTS vice president (1994–95), policy chair (1996–2005) and president-elect (2006).{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}} In 2004 Baldwin was awarded the Australian Government [[Eureka Prizes|Eureka Prize]] for Promoting Understanding of Science, for his role in initiating and championing "Science meets Parliament".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://australianmuseum.net.au/eureka-past|title=Past Winners & Finalists (Eureka Prizes) - Australian Museum|website=australianmuseum.net.au|access-date=2016-05-17}}</ref> This annual event comprises meetings between hundreds of scientists and politicians and is supported by Federal government funding.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://scienceandtechnologyaustralia.org.au/science-meets-parliament/|title=Science meets Parliament|date=2014-12-03|website=Science & Technology Australia|language=en-US|access-date=2016-05-17}}</ref> His contributions to Public Policy at ANU were recognised in 2012 by the award of one of nine inaugural ANU Public Policy Fellowships.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://vcdesk.anu.edu.au/2012/04/13/enhancing-public-policy-at-anu/|title=Enhancing Public Policy at ANU - From the Vice-Chancellor's desk - ANU|access-date=2016-05-17}}</ref>

In 2014 he received the ANU Vice Chancellor's award for Enhancing the Reputation of the University.{{cn|date=November 2024}}

== Energy policy ==
Through his role as Director of the ANU Energy Change Institute, Baldwin has contributed to national energy policy, including through ECI submissions to:
* The 2012 Energy Green Paper 
* Emissions abatement options for Australia: assessments against criteria of magnitude, cost and quality 2014 
* Review of the Renewable Energy Target 2014
* The 2014 Energy Green Paper
In 2012 Baldwin initiated Energy Update,{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}} the ECI's annual flagship event at which the [[International Energy Agency]] presents the latest [[World Energy Outlook]], critiqued by a series of discussion panels.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://energy.anu.edu.au/news-events/anu-energy-update-presents-world-energy-outlook-2013|title=ANU Energy Update presents the World Energy Outlook 2013|date=2013-11-01|website=ECI|access-date=2016-05-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://energy.anu.edu.au/news-events/2015-anu-energy-update|title=2015 ANU Energy Update|date=2015-12-22|website=ECI|access-date=2016-05-17}}</ref> This is in addition to numerous other ECI public events, such as those providing public discussion forums on the Federal government's Energy White Papers.

Since 2011 Baldwin has been a member of the Project Steering Committee for the Australian Energy Technology Assessment (AETA) produced by the Bureau of Resources and Energy Economics (BREE).<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.industry.gov.au/Office-of-the-Chief-Economist/Publications/Documents/aeta/australian_energy_technology_assessment.pdf|title=Australia Energy Technology Assessment 2012|publisher=Australian Government Bureau of Resources & Energy Economics|year=2012|isbn=978-1-922106-29-2|location=Canberra, Australia|pages=iii}}</ref>  In 2015, he was appointed as a member of the Socio-Economic Modelling Advisory Committee to the South Australian [[Nuclear Fuel Cycle Royal Commission]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nuclearrc.sa.gov.au/disclosure-of-potentially-relevant-roles-interests-socio-economic-modelling-advisory-committee/|title=Disclosure of Potentially Relevant Roles & Interests – Socio-Economic Modelling Advisory Committee|publisher=Nuclear Fuel Cycle Royal Commission|access-date=2016-05-17|archive-date=10 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610192610/http://nuclearrc.sa.gov.au/disclosure-of-potentially-relevant-roles-interests-socio-economic-modelling-advisory-committee/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Nuclear power commentary ==
Baldwin has also commented on [[nuclear power in Australia]]. Following the announcement of the [[Nuclear Fuel Cycle Royal Commission]] in South Australia in February 2015, Baldwin told the [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC]]:<blockquote>Australia is an energy rich country... we have 40 per cent of the worlds [[uranium]] stock, so it makes enormous sense for us to look at to replacing our fossil fuels with renewables and also with the prospect of using our vast quantities of [[nuclear power]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = SA royal commission on nuclear energy sparks calls for discussion to go national| website=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]] |url = http://www.abc.net.au/worldtoday/content/2015/s4176304.htm|date = 2015-02-09|access-date = 2015-06-24}}</ref></blockquote>In June 2015 Baldwin told the ''Science Show'' on ABC Radio National that "the use of nuclear power to generate electricity is going to be carbon free". Professor Baldwin also speculated on the prospect of nuclear industrial development in Australia, stating:<blockquote>It's these two things—social licence and a regulatory framework—that really need a lot of attention in the near future if we are going to have a nuclear industry in this country. It will involve a process that could take a considerable period of time.</blockquote>Baldwin also commented on the changing nature of the electricity market in Australia, and pointed to some uncertainty around the economics of nuclear power.<blockquote>The price of renewables is dropping, solar is dropping much faster than wind. And it could well be that by 15 years' time solar is really in a position to be the leading form of new power generation. If we wait too long then the nuclear option might have gone completely.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Geothermal and nuclear energy|url = http://www.abc.net.au/radionational/programs/scienceshow/energy-futures---part-1-of-4/6535408|website = Radio National|access-date = 2015-06-24}}</ref></blockquote>
* [http://www.policyforum.net/could-nuclear-be-a-power-of-good/ "Nuclear could be a power of good", ''PolicyForum.net'' and Advance (2014).]
* {{cite news |last=Baldwin |first=Ken |title=What role will Australia have on the nuclear world stage? |date=11 May 2016 |work=[[The Age]] |url=https://www.theage.com.au/opinion/what-role-will-australia-have-on-the-nuclear-world-stage-20160510-goqg6n.html}}
